abstract.text: For 2026 WattClarity news and AEMO market notices in Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM), we test whether language-model extractions improve on nested references holding the numerical inputs and text activity, in a retrospective out-of-sample evaluation locked by trusted timestamps before scoring, conditional on saved versions, declared availability clocks and the pre-specified learner and information set. Price-only LEAR changed the numerical reference's error by -21.3% in 2025 and -22.140% (a reliable improvement) in 2026; 2025 news labels changed it by +0.18% (p = 0.61). For day-ahead news, article activity changed the numerical reference's error by -3.578% (a reliable improvement); against it, the label-count representation changed the error by +11.412% (no reliable increment detected; fragile: one-day interval disagreed, three-seed mean not available; not fully checked: three-seed mean unavailable); the structured-attribute embedding changed the error by +1.171% (no reliable increment detected; not fully checked: three-seed mean unavailable); improvements above 3.443% were excluded (family-adjusted, one-sided 1.25%), below the 3.8% literature reference value; at the Monte Carlo resolution of 2,000 bootstrap draws this bound cannot be placed on one side of the 3.8% literature reference value, too imprecise to separate the 0.18% and 0.32% 2025 news effects from zero. For market notices (creation-date surrogate clocks), against notice activity, the event-state representation changed the error by -0.303% (a reliable increment; inferentially robust; an increment over notice activity only; interval wholly below 0.5%; persisted when each forecast was averaged equally with the pre-dispatch-price reference, combination inferentially robust); the message, failure and fuel-group counts changed the error by -0.284% (a primary-seed increment; fragile: three-seed mean disagreed, three-seed mean no reliable increment detected; attribution and comparison-value classes not assigned; averaged equally with the pre-dispatch-price reference: a reliable increment, combination fragile); the structured-attribute notice embedding changed the error by -0.747% (a reliable increment; inferentially robust; an increment over notice activity only; point above 0.5%, interval straddling it; persisted when each forecast was averaged equally with the pre-dispatch-price reference, combination inferentially robust).

conclusion_core: For day-ahead news, article activity changed the numerical reference's error by -3.578% [-6.396, -0.866] (a reliable improvement); against it, the label-count representation changed the error by +11.412% [1.220, 26.787] (no reliable increment detected; fragile: one-day interval disagreed, three-seed mean not available; not fully checked: three-seed mean unavailable); the structured-attribute embedding changed the error by +1.171% [-3.298, 5.625] (no reliable increment detected; not fully checked: three-seed mean unavailable); improvements larger than 3.443% were excluded at the family-adjusted one-sided 1.25% level, below the 3.8% literature reference value; at the Monte Carlo resolution of 2,000 bootstrap draws this bound cannot be placed on one side of the 3.8% literature reference value, but this window cannot distinguish effects as small as the 2025 news contrasts (0.18% and 0.32%) from zero.

For market notices (creation-date surrogate clocks), against notice activity, the event-state representation changed the error by -0.303% [-0.403, -0.201] (a reliable increment of 0.0287 AUD/MWh; inferentially robust; an increment over notice activity only; interval wholly below the 0.5% historical-effect reference; persisted when each forecast was averaged equally with the pre-dispatch-price reference, combination inferentially robust); the message, failure and fuel-group counts changed the error by -0.284% [-0.398, -0.165] (a primary-seed increment of 0.0269 AUD/MWh; fragile: three-seed mean disagreed, three-seed mean -0.004% [-0.054, 0.049], no reliable increment detected; attribution and comparison-value classes not assigned; averaged equally with the pre-dispatch-price reference: a reliable increment, combination fragile); the structured-attribute notice embedding changed the error by -0.747% [-1.019, -0.473] (a reliable increment of 0.0706 AUD/MWh; inferentially robust; an increment over notice activity only; point above the 0.5% historical-effect reference, interval straddling it; persisted when each forecast was averaged equally with the pre-dispatch-price reference, combination inferentially robust).

Against the pre-specified cheap-text representations of the same notices (secondary, unadjusted), the event-state representation did not outperform the rule parser and performed reliably worse than the word-frequency representation: not better than the pre-specified cheap-text representations.

Against the pre-specified cheap-text representations of the same notices (secondary, unadjusted), the message, failure and fuel-group counts did not outperform the rule parser and performed reliably worse than the word-frequency representation: not better than the pre-specified cheap-text representations.

Against the same representation built from content shifted by 28 days, the structured-attribute notice embedding changed the error by -0.745% (95% interval [-0.995, -0.492]%, DM p < 0.001 on the 38 shift-supported days): a reliable improvement; this secondary reading changes activity timing together with content, so it is not an attribution level.

Against the pre-specified cheap-text representations of the same notices (secondary, unadjusted), the structured-attribute notice embedding outperformed the rule parser and the word-frequency representation: better than the pre-specified cheap-text representations.

These readings are relative to the pre-specified learner and information set: the primary news reference uses no operator forecasts and the primary notice reference uses no five-minute pre-dispatch prices.

Price-only LEAR changed the numerical reference's mean absolute error by -21.3% in 2025 (39.73 against 50.51 AUD/MWh) and by -22.140% [-27.544, -16.739] (a reliable improvement) in the 2026 news window; in an internally pre-specified 2025 test, adding extracted news labels changed it by +0.18%.
Because the absolute-error family was not completed, the news readings are specific to the squared-error training objective.
Because the pre-dispatch family was not completed, the news readings are specific to an information set without operator forecasts.
No reading here is a causal effect, a verified real-time trading gain or a cost comparison.
execution_sentence: Of the 16 pre-specified fitting and scoring stages (Supplement Table {table_ref}), 5 completed fully, 2 completed apart from recorded unavailable configurations, 4 were not run, 0 deviated from the frozen design and 5 had no result when this version was filled; the predictions of every completed stage were fixed before that stage's scoring read confirmation prices, and the planted-signal check uses pre-confirmation data only.
methods_sentences: The comparison values are interpretation aids and never enter a decision. For news, the literature reference value is 3.8% of the reference error, the smallest text-attributed error reduction with a significance test in the cited electricity forecasting work (day-ahead load, text against no text); it is a published comparison value, not a smallest effect of practical interest for price content beyond activity. For notices, the comparison value is 0.5% of the reference error: the equivalence tolerance of the earlier January–February 2026 notice test (window C), used here as a historical-effect reference; that tolerance was set after development results were known and is not an economic indifference threshold.

A reading is inferentially robust when the one-day and seven-day bootstrap intervals, the small-sample HLN calibration, the HAC7 long-run variance and the three-seed mean all agree with its decision class; a pre-specified design sensitivity with a different decision class is reported beside it as a design dissent. Attribution, comparison-value classes and the persistence wording of the combination check are given only to inferentially robust increments; a fragile or not fully checked increment is reported as a primary-seed increment together with the three-seed mean's estimate, family-adjusted interval and decision class.

Content-specific attribution cannot be reached in this design, and no increment is described as specific to the language model. For notices, the activity-matched reassignment control has no matched key by construction; for news, its matched keys, computed before scoring from the input-side mask, cover 216 of 15,408 keys (1.4%) on 3 of 214 days, fewer than the seven days its frozen secondary rule requires, so it is not evaluable. Every reliable increment is therefore described as an increment over its activity reference; the 28-day shift comparison and the comparison with the pre-specified cheap-text representations are reported beside it as secondary readings. All comparisons are predictive, not causal.
Statement-level proportions are descriptive: their judgements cluster within articles, so no interval is given.

Improvements larger than 3.443% of the reference error were excluded at the family-adjusted one-sided 1.25% level, conditional on these fitted predictions; this bound is below the 3.8% literature reference value, so improvements of that size are excluded by this window; at the Monte Carlo resolution of 2,000 bootstrap draws this bound cannot be placed on one side of the 3.8% literature reference value.
The activity-matched reassignment control found matched keys on only 3 days, too few for the frozen seven-day rule, so the primary contrasts are not recomputed on its support.
Against the numerical reference, article activity changed the error by -3.578% (0.8878 AUD/MWh lower; unadjusted 95% interval [-6.396, -0.866]%, DM p = 0.017): a reliable improvement.

For each structured representation, improvements larger than 3.443% of the reference error were excluded at the family-adjusted one-sided 1.25% level, which is below the 3.8% literature reference value.
Text activity therefore improved reliably on the numerical reference, while no reliable increment of a structured representation over text activity was detected.

This bound is at or above the design's minimum detectable effect of 3.11% and at or above both of the 0.18% and 0.32% magnitudes of the 2025 news contrasts; with a power of 2.7% at 0.32%, this window cannot distinguish effects of that size from zero.

Against the numerical reference, the label-count representation changed the error by +7.425% (unadjusted 95% interval [-2.670, 20.573]%; no reliable difference detected), the structured-attribute embedding by -2.449% ([-6.922, 2.089]%; no reliable difference detected) and the article activity reference by -3.578% ([-6.396, -0.866]%; a reliable improvement); Table {table_ref} places these text-versus-no-text estimates beside the published no-text-to-text comparisons, whose relative error changes computed from the reported metric pairs range from a 1.37% increase to a 13.90% reduction.

In the 2026 news window, price-only LEAR changed the error of the numerical reference by -22.140% (5.4937 AUD/MWh lower; unadjusted 95% interval [-27.544, -16.739]%, DM p < 0.001): a reliable improvement; in 2025 it changed it by -21.3%.
The planted-signal check was not run for day-ahead news (no result was available at the time of the fill); the sensitivity of the test pipeline is not documented for this task.

For notices, the activity-matched reassignment control has no matched key by construction: each notice representation encodes the full saved prefix, so an earlier prefix with the same count contains the same notices, which the donor rule excludes; the notice content-specific label therefore cannot be reached.
